south-america.name: Atacama Desert
south-america.note: Driest non-polar desert on Earth — the cold Peruvian (Humboldt) Current offshore cools the air, suppressing evaporation, so little moisture ever reaches it as rain; some stations have never recorded any.

south-america.name: Pampas
south-america.note: Fertile temperate grassland — Argentina's agricultural heartland (beef cattle, wheat, soy); alfalfa is a key fodder crop.

south-america.name: Patagonia
south-america.note: Windswept plateau/steppe in the Andes' rain shadow — the Pacific westerlies drop their moisture on Chile's windward coast, leaving Argentina's leeward side arid; also called a Piedmont plateau (built up at the mountains' foothills) or, for its climate, the Patagonian Desert.

south-america.name: Gran Chaco
south-america.note: Vast lowland plain of scrub and grassland spanning Paraguay, Argentina and Bolivia — divided into northern, southern and middle sectors.

south-america.name: Altiplano
south-america.note: High Andean inter-montane plateau (~3,750 m average) between the eastern and western Andes — also called the Bolivian Plateau; second-largest such plateau after Tibet's.

south-america.name: Llanos
south-america.note: Seasonally flooded tropical grassland plains either side of the Orinoco, shared between Venezuela and Colombia — used for cattle ranching.

south-america.name: Selvas (Amazon Basin)
south-america.note: Selvas — the evergreen equatorial rainforest of the Amazon basin; most of it lies within Brazil, with the rest across Peru and Colombia.

south-america.name: Caatinga
south-america.note: Semi-arid thorn-scrub forest of NE Brazil — drought-adapted vegetation and one of the country's most biodiverse dry-forest biomes.

south-america.name: Cerrado
south-america.note: Brazil's vast tropical savanna — wooded grassland covering roughly a fifth of the country; a major soy frontier and biodiversity hotspot.

south-america.name: Campos
south-america.note: Grassland region of NE/SE Brazil supporting cattle ranching, graded locally into campos limpos, sujos and cerrados by vegetation density.

south-america.name: Borborema Plateau
south-america.note: Crystalline plateau of NE Brazil, between the coast and the semi-arid Caatinga interior.

south-america.name: Mato Grosso Plateau
south-america.note: Central Brazilian plateau and major watershed divide, feeding both the Amazon and the Paraná/Plata river systems; a soybean frontier.

north-america.name: Great Plains
north-america.note: Vast interior grassland — the US/Canada 'breadbasket', once home to vast bison herds.

north-america.name: Colorado Plateau
north-america.note: High sedimentary plateau carved by rivers into the Grand Canyon.

north-america.name: Mojave Desert
north-america.note: Home to Death Valley, the hottest and lowest point in North America.

north-america.name: Sonoran Desert
north-america.note: Shared with the southwestern US; known for the iconic saguaro cactus.

north-america.name: Canadian Prairies
north-america.note: Wheat-growing plains across Alberta, Saskatchewan and Manitoba.

africa.name: Sahara Desert
africa.note: World's largest hot desert, spanning most of North Africa across ~11 countries.

africa.name: East African savanna
africa.note: Grassland/savanna supporting the Great Migration across the Serengeti–Mara ecosystem.

africa.name: Ethiopian Highlands
africa.note: 'Roof of Africa' — source of the Blue Nile, shaped by the Great Rift Valley.

africa.name: Kalahari Desert
africa.note: Semi-arid sandy savanna spanning South Africa, Botswana and Namibia.

africa.name: Highveld
africa.note: High interior plateau (~1,500 m) where Johannesburg and Pretoria sit.

europe.name: Pontic Steppe
europe.note: Fertile black-soil (chernozem) grassland — historic invasion corridor and grain belt.

europe.name: Meseta Central
europe.note: High interior plateau covering much of Spain, where Madrid sits.

europe.name: Scandinavian Mountains (fjord plateau)
europe.note: Glacially carved highlands behind Norway's fjord coastline.

asia.name: Rub' al Khali (Empty Quarter)
asia.note: Largest contiguous sand desert in the world.

asia.name: Gobi Desert
asia.note: Cold desert spanning southern Mongolia and northern China.

asia.name: Tibetan Plateau
asia.note: 'Roof of the World' (~4,500 m average) — source of Asia's major rivers.

asia.name: Kazakh Steppe
asia.note: One of the world's largest dry steppe regions, historic Silk Road corridor.

asia.name: Thar Desert
asia.note: Great Indian Desert along the India–Pakistan border, in Rajasthan.

asia.name: Deccan Plateau
asia.note: Triangular volcanic plateau covering most of peninsular India.

australia-oceania.name: Great Victoria Desert
australia-oceania.note: Australia's largest desert, spanning Western Australia and South Australia.

australia-oceania.name: Nullarbor Plain
australia-oceania.note: Vast, almost treeless limestone plateau along the southern coast.
